channel.title: The Talas Herald
channel.description: News from Talas and across Irad.

item.title: Nurzhan Compute Park: $450m, 40 MW rising to 150 MW, but partners unnamed
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor toured the gas-fired data-centre site on Monday and promised 300 jobs; gas volumes, cooling water and who pays for the grid link were not given.

item.title: Kervan Elektrik to run Nurzhan, Chu and Kara-Buura grids; loss target is 11%
item.description: The Turkish operator, already running Talas, takes over metering and billing under a 15-year contract, while the utility keeps the wires and Toktogul revenue stays outside the deal.

item.title: Heat plant gas conversions would put IS 670 million on Talas and Nurzhan bills
item.description: University sensors logged 71 days above an alert level in Nurzhan's Dastgoh last winter, yet private-house stoves are outside the plan.

item.title: Kyrgyz FDI of $1.3bn is 4.5 times Irad's inflow, Bank of Irad figures show
item.description: Most of the ISEZ's US$286 million in 2025 went to energy and minerals, and over half was reinvested profit from firms already here.

item.title: Draft ban on potato imports to 1 March tests whether the record crop will keep
item.description: Imports were under 7% of last year's supply, ministry figures show, but they arrived in the late-winter weeks when stored local stocks run short.

item.title: EU grants Kyrgyzstan €6m for school reforms, paid on results
item.description: The budget support, about 592 million Kyrgyz som, goes to the treasury in Bishkek; the ISEZ has no EU channel of its own, though many Iradi families use Kyrgyz schools.

item.title: Name the partners before public money goes into Sary-Bulak
item.description: The antimony restart is welcome news for the district, but two sets of official figures disagree and IS 114 million rests on backers nobody will name.

item.title: First business census runs to 30 November; bazaar stalls and farms are the test
item.description: Officials put the unobserved economy at 23% of output and 60% of farm turnover, and firms must answer or face fines.

item.title: Kyrgyz fish plant opens near Bishkek with 3,000-tonne capacity
item.description: Talas traders say the Alamudun plant matters less for its size than for who owns the cold chain between Chui region and the Kichi-Korgon crossing.

item.title: Kyrgyz fuel output up 1.9-fold; Irad's diesel still rests on one refinery
item.description: Bishkek's statistics show a near doubling in nine months, but no public record shows any of it reaching ISEZ pumps, where bus fares rise on Monday.

item.title: Kyrgyz building output up 1.6-fold; Talas permits rose 13%, costs 18%
item.description: Bishkek's statisticians report a construction surge, while Talas planning records show a smaller rise in approvals and a steeper one in the price of finishing a flat.

item.title: Record harvest of 210,000 tonnes of potatoes leaves growers paid less than bazaar prices suggest
item.description: Grain output is up about 40 per cent on 2025 at 1.2 million tonnes, but storage, not supply, will decide who gains from the glut, growers and an economist say.

item.title: Bishkek revives metro plan despite its own planners' cost and demand finding
item.description: Talas economists say the dispute is a lesson in who pays for rail transit in a city of about a million people, and no Iradi budget could carry one.

item.title: Sary-Bulak restart needs IS 168 million and 420 hires in first stage
item.description: Budget and company papers put the state's share at IS 54 million, while the partners and the smelter's start date remain open.

item.title: Potato import halt could add IS 0.60 a kilo by January, Bazar-i Kalan traders say
item.description: The ministry says a pause until March would stop a harvest-time price slump; wholesalers say shoppers would pay for it once stores run low.

item.title: Customs roadmap with Kazakhstan puts scanner costs on ISEZ budget and carriers
item.description: The 2027–2028 plan promises electronic pre-clearance at Talas North Terminal, but a per-truck fee is still in a draft tariff schedule.

item.title: Sary-Bulak's 13 new plants create 138 jobs, but only 91 are year-round
item.description: District records show two small hydro stations account for IS 22 million of IS 58.6 million invested and employ seven people between them.

item.title: Toktogul's extra 240 MW raises the question of who shares the revenue
item.description: All four units now run at 360 MW, but the cost of the refit and the formula that divides export income remain unpublished.

item.title: Antimony restart relies on partners the combine has not named
item.description: About IS 125 million is to reopen idled lines at Sary-Bulak and Chatkal; a mercury unit at the smelter will need a new permit and a public hearing.

item.title: Court adjourns Tulparcoin name case to November without an injunction
item.description: Judge Asel Mamytbekova asked both sides whether a cryptocurrency is a "financial service" at all, and gave them five weeks to answer.

item.title: Tashkent calls water scarcity a brake on the region as Naryn talks near
item.description: Uzbekistan's president urged digital monitoring and canal repairs at a summit in Turkmenistan; Irad's negotiators say the 2027 Naryn schedule will need the same data.

item.title: Rabat-i-Safed coins to be tested in Nurzhan as museum asks for custody
item.description: The heritage permit for the dig says finds go to the national museum; the university wants to keep the Kara-Khanid coins until its study is published.

item.title: Thirty new schools deserve one published budget
item.description: The building programme is welcome. Its total cost and its timetable should be public.

item.title: Attelkom blocks Tulparcoin sites; operator cites Department of Public Information list
item.description: The coin's website and its Seychelles exchange became unreachable on Thursday; the department says it acted on a request from "financial supervisors".

item.title: Supreme Court puts its case register online; inability petition awaits a date
item.description: The new public docket lists 214 pending matters, among them the June petition on the Elective Governor Acts, marked as awaiting listing.

item.title: Komuz contest is open to highland players, if they can get travel permits
item.description: The rules for the Aigul Choro kyzy competition welcome entrants from across the line, but clan permits must be registered with the Gendarmerie before 22 October.

item.title: Boztorgoy and Karakoyun stay perfect as ulak league reaches round four
item.description: In Talas a Chicago-born fighter rode with the city team in training, but Directorate rules keep unlicensed guests out of league play.

item.title: Navbahor school cost IS 31.5 million, council papers show
item.description: The solar-roofed school opened by the Lieutenant Governor on Monday is one of 30 due this year, but the programme's total budget has not been published.

item.title: Prosecutors ask court to wind up 16 trade-zone firms over sanctions risk
item.description: The applications follow a review of about 40 companies by the Foreign Trade Escrow Authority, and Talasbank has closed the accounts of some 120 firms.

item.title: Ministry proposes halting potato imports until March as harvest outruns demand
item.description: Growers in the Talas valley welcome the draft, but the self-sufficiency rate it cites does not match the ministry's own forecasts.
